vulnerabilities.description: Insecure file permissions: JSON memory files created with default umask (likely 0644). Sensitive session/context data may be world-readable. Should use fs.writeFileSync(MEMORY_FILE, data, { mode: 0o600 }) to restrict to owner-only access.
Insecure file permissions: Session files created with default umask. Files contain context data and metrics that could be sensitive. Should explicitly set file mode to 0o600 (owner-only read/write).

Prototype pollution risk: User-supplied keys (e.g., '__proto__', 'constructor') could potentially modify object prototypes. Mitigated by JSON serialization but should validate keys against a whitelist or reject special names.

Silent cleanup of temporary files: Empty catch block ignores cleanup failures which could leave sensitive body content in /tmp. Should log or handle cleanup errors, or use try-finally with explicit error handling.
No input validation on session keys: update() method accepts arbitrary key names without validation. Could create invalid JSON keys or namespace collisions.

recommendations: Set explicit file permissions (0o600) for all sensitive files: memory.js:22, session.js:21. Example: fs.writeFileSync(path, JSON.stringify(data), { mode: 0o600 })
Validate/whitelist memory and session keys to prevent prototype pollution and namespace issues
Handle temporary file cleanup errors explicitly in github-safe.js rather than silently ignoring them
Add encryption for sensitive context/session data at rest, or document security assumptions
Review .claude-flow/data/ and .claude-flow/sessions/ directories to ensure restrictive permissions
No hardcoded secrets, SQL injection, or XSS vulnerabilities detected in provided code
Ensure Node.js dependencies in package.json are regularly audited (file not provided - cannot assess)
